title: The Vvaan Day 14: ₹86 Crore Worldwide, Less Than ₹3 Crore From a Career Milestone
excerpt: Sidharth Malhotra and Tamannaah Bhatia's folklore thriller has grossed ₹85.61 crore worldwide through day 13, per trade estimates, and is closing in on the next rung of Malhotra's all-time career chart.
body:
• The Vvaan has grossed an estimated ₹85.61 crore worldwide through 13 days — ₹66.31 crore net in India plus ₹7.35 crore overseas — according to trade estimates compiled by Koimoi.
  • The film is now Sidharth Malhotra's sixth-highest-grossing film globally, having overtaken Marjaavaan (₹65.34 crore), and is within striking distance of Param Sundari (₹89.72 crore), the next title above it on his career chart.
  • Trade watchers credit the Chhath Puja backdrop and strong heartland turnout — Bihar advance sales led the country, an unusual feat for the circuit.
  • The film remains in theatres in India and overseas territories with no streaming date announced yet; diaspora readers can check local listings for showtimes.

A steady run into the third week

The Vvaan: Force of the Forest, the folklore fantasy thriller starring Sidharth Malhotra and Tamannaah Bhatia, is holding its ground at the box office well into its third week. According to trade estimates compiled by Koimoi, the film earned ₹85.61 crore in worldwide gross through its 13th day — ₹66.31 crore net (₹78.26 crore gross) at the Indian box office, supplemented by ₹7.35 crore from overseas territories.

The day-wise pattern tells the story of a film carried by a strong opening weekend and an unusually resilient heartland audience. The film opened on September 25 to roughly ₹8 crore on day one, jumped to ₹11.25 crore on Saturday and ₹14 crore on Sunday, for a ₹33.25-crore opening weekend, per Sacnilk figures reported by iDiva. Trade analyst Taran Adarsh flagged the surge at the time, writing that mass pockets and the Hindi heartland had delivered “excellent business.”

Weekday holds in the second week were modest — day 10 brought ₹3.25 crore net, day 11 just ₹0.95 crore — but the film kept screens alive even as new competition arrived, including an Avengers: Endgame re-release and The Paradise.

Climbing Malhotra's career chart

The run has quietly become one of the more notable commercial stories of Malhotra's career. Per Koimoi's published career chart, the actor's all-time worldwide leaders are Ek Villain (₹169.62 crore), Kapoor & Sons (₹147.94 crore), Brothers (₹140.3 crore), Student of the Year (₹109.1 crore) and Param Sundari (₹89.72 crore). The Vvaan has already passed Marjaavaan, Hasee Toh Phasee and Baar Baar Dekho to sit at No. 6 — and Koimoi's latest update puts it less than ₹3 crore from overtaking Param Sundari for the No. 5 spot.

“The Vvaan takes a big step forward, hitting double digits on Saturday, with the mass pockets and heartland delivering excellent business.”

— Taran Adarsh, trade analyst

The film is also a banner milestone: Koimoi reports it is the fourth-highest-grossing venture ever for Balaji Motion Pictures, the studio that produced it jointly with TVF Motion Pictures. For Tamannaah Bhatia, the film has become her second-highest-grossing Bollywood project, according to Zoom TV.

The Chhath factor

One of the more unusual threads in the film's run is geography. Pinkvilla reported that advance sales in Bihar — a circuit whose exhibition infrastructure has thinned dramatically over the years — were running ahead of Delhi and Mumbai, something the trade press called nearly unprecedented. The driver: the film is rooted in Chhath Puja folklore, the harvest festival that dominates Bihar's cultural calendar, and its mythology-inflected story of local legends appears to have resonated directly with that audience.

That regional strength matters commercially. As FilmiMagic noted, the film's theatrical lifetime is expected to land around ₹65–70 crore net in India — a modest figure by blockbuster standards, but a genuine success for a mid-budget folklore thriller that, as Pinkvilla observed, looked “destined to be a non-starter” a month before release.

What comes next

The immediate question is whether The Vvaan can close the roughly ₹3-crore gap to Param Sundari before screens contract further. Daily collections have tapered to the ₹0.8–1.5 crore range, so the milestone will likely need another full weekend of holds. Trade watchers at NewsDIO project a final worldwide tally in the ₹85–90 crore band, which the film has now entered.

For Malhotra, whose post-COVID theatrical record has been uneven, the film is already his second-biggest grosser of the post-pandemic era. Whether it takes the No. 5 career spot or stalls just short, The Vvaan has given both its lead star and its banner a genuine theatrical win in a year when mid-budget Hindi films have struggled to find audiences.
